assertions.description: AudioWorklet.prototype exposes the port attribute (the exact IDL member this feature adds).
AudioWorklet.port is a readonly attribute: an accessor with a getter and no setter on AudioWorklet.prototype.
assertions.test: (() => { const d = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(AudioWorklet.prototype, 'port'); return !!d && typeof d.get === 'function' && d.set === undefined; })()

assertions.description: audioWorklet.port is a MessagePort immediately after the context is constructed, before any addModule() call (the channel is created in the BaseAudioContext constructor; checked on an OfflineAudioContext).
Reading audioWorklet.port twice returns the same MessagePort object.
assertions.test: (() => { const w = new OfflineAudioContext(1, 128, 8000).audioWorklet; return w.port instanceof MessagePort && w.port === w.port; })()

assertions.description: Each BaseAudioContext gets its own channel: two contexts' audioWorklet.port objects are distinct MessagePorts.
assertions.test: (() => { const a = new OfflineAudioContext(1, 128, 8000).audioWorklet.port; const b = new OfflineAudioContext(1, 128, 8000).audioWorklet.port; return a instanceof MessagePort && b instanceof MessagePort && a !== b; })()

assertions.description: Inside the AudioWorkletGlobalScope, the global port is a MessagePort during module evaluation and can post to the main thread with no AudioWorkletNode created.
assertions.test: (async () => { const c = new OfflineAudioContext(1, 128, 8000); const p = c.audioWorklet.port; if (!(p instanceof MessagePort)) return false; const src = 'port.postMessage({ scopePortIsMessagePort: (typeof port === "object") && (port instanceof MessagePort) });'; const got = new Promise((resolve) => { const t = setTimeout(() => resolve(false), 2000); p.onmessage = (e) => { clearTimeout(t); resolve(e.data && e.data.scopePortIsMessagePort === true); }; }); await c.audioWorklet.addModule(URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([src], { type: 'text/javascript' }))); return await got; })()

assertions.description: A message posted on audioWorklet.port is received by the global scope's port and its reply arrives back on audioWorklet.port.
assertions.test: (async () => { const c = new OfflineAudioContext(1, 128, 8000); const p = c.audioWorklet.port; if (!(p instanceof MessagePort)) return false; const src = 'port.onmessage = (e) => port.postMessage({ echo: e.data });'; await c.audioWorklet.addModule(URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([src], { type: 'text/javascript' }))); return await new Promise((resolve) => { const t = setTimeout(() => resolve(false), 2000); p.onmessage = (e) => { clearTimeout(t); resolve(e.data && e.data.echo === 'conformance-ping'); }; p.postMessage('conformance-ping'); }); })()

assertions.description: Messages posted on audioWorklet.port before addModule() are queued and delivered, in order, once the module sets port.onmessage. (manual: spec does not pin global-scope creation timing; unverified on a supporting build)
assertions.test: Not asserted automatically: the Web Audio spec text (1.32.1 / 1.32.3) says only that the port is connected to the AudioWorkletGlobalScope port and does not say when the global scope is created, so delivery of messages posted before addModule() is implementation-defined until verified on a build with AudioWorkletSharedPort. Observe it on /v159/shared-messageport-for-audioworklet/port-edge-cases/.

assertions.description: The existing per-node channel is unaffected: AudioWorkletNode.prototype still exposes port (the shared port is additive).
